name: Seated Calf Raise — Toes Angled In
description: A seated calf raise performed with the toes angled inward (pigeon-toed position), which shifts the emphasis toward the outer head of the gastrocnemius and the lateral soleus fibers. The seated position places the knee at 90 degrees of flexion, reducing gastrocnemius contribution and increasing soleus activation relative to a standing variation. This variation is used in calf rehabilitation and strength programs targeting specific fiber imbalances.

execution.starting_position: Sit on a bench or chair with feet flat on the floor or on an edge for greater ROM. Turn the toes inward (internally rotate the feet) approximately 15-30 degrees. Rest a dumbbell or plate on each thigh if adding resistance.
execution.setup_instructions: Use a flat bench with a plate on the thigh for resistance, or a dedicated seated calf raise machine. Position the balls of the feet on the edge of a step if greater stretch is desired.
steps: Step 1: Sit tall with toes turned inward and feet positioned on the edge for full range.
Step 2: Lower the heels as far as comfortable to achieve a full dorsiflexion stretch.
Step 3: Press through the balls of the feet to rise onto the toes, achieving full plantarflexion.
Step 4: Lower back down under control. Repeat.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you rise onto the toes. Inhale as you lower.
common_mistakes: Using partial range — not achieving full stretch at the bottom
Bouncing at the bottom rather than controlling the eccentric
Rotating the entire lower leg rather than just turning toes in
safety_considerations: If you experience lateral knee discomfort with toes-in position, reduce the angle of inward rotation
Avoid with acute Achilles tendinopathy — consult a physiotherapist
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full range: from maximum dorsiflexion (heel at or below forefoot level) to maximum plantarflexion (full toe rise).
execution.tempo_recommendations: 2-1-2-1 (2s lower, 1s stretch, 2s rise, 1s squeeze at top)
coaching_cues: Let the heel drop below the forefoot to get the full stretch
Squeeze the outer calf at the top of each rep
Keep the knee angle constant — do not straighten the leg during the movement
